basis.title: Energy Conservation Program for Certain Industrial Equipment: Energy Conservation Standards for Small, Large, and Very Large Air-Cooled Commercial Package Air Conditioning and Heating Equipment and Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (direct final rule), 81 FR 2420, January 15, 2016
basis.label: "the average lifetime of the equipment, which is estimated to be 23 years for both gas-fired and oil-fired CWAFs"
basis.note: Printed page 2423. class: commercial warm air furnaces >=225,000 Btu/h input, gas-fired and oil-fired. Commercial, mostly weatherized/rooftop-mounted; residential furnaces are covered separately (consumer furnace rule). Lifetime derived from the CUAC lifetime (section IV.F.6.b, p.60, printed 2479).

basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Furnaces (final rule), 88 FR 87502, December 18, 2023
basis.label: "DOE estimates the average product lifetime to be 21.5 years for NWGFs and MHGFs"
basis.note: Printed page 87571. residential: non-weatherized gas furnaces and mobile home gas furnaces; national average. Regional averages 22.5 years (North) and 20.2 years (rest of country) in the same paragraph. Also p.2 (printed 87503).

basis.title: Purchasing Energy-Efficient Residential Furnaces (web page, modified 2026-09-25)
basis.by: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Energy Management Program
basis.label: Lifetime Energy Cost: Assumed an average residential furnace lifetime of 21 years.
basis.note: Residential furnaces under 225,000 Btu/h (FEMP scope covers natural gas, propane and oil); the examples are 70,000 Btu/h gas furnaces at 80-99% AFUE, Northern and Southern regions. Commercial furnaces are not covered.

open_questions: Every source here is a published planning, design or accounting life. None is observed replacement data.
Furnace tasks come from Army TM 5-642 (1990); equipment and practice may have changed since.
